title: Adding and Taking Away to 10
seo_title: Foundation Addition and Subtraction Worksheets: Adding and Taking Away to 10 (Free, with Answers)
standard_text: Represent practical situations involving addition, subtraction and quantification with physical and virtual materials and use counting or subitising strategies.
meta_desc: Free Foundation (Prep, Kindergarten) maths worksheets on adding and taking away to 10, matched to the Australian Curriculum (AC9MFN05): join groups, take away, count on and back on a number line, and everyday stories. 100 picture questions with answers.
key_big: Adding makes the group bigger. Taking away makes it smaller.
key_sub: Count on from the first number to add. Count what is left to take away.
body_html:
Adding: join and count on

When more things come, the group gets bigger. Start with the first number and count on.

Taking away: what is left?

When things go away, the group gets smaller. Cross them out and count the rest.

Use a number line

Hop forward to add. Hop back to take away. Do not count the number you start on.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do
Counting the starting number againStart on the number, then count the hops
Giving the number taken awayCount the ones that are left
Adding when things go awayAsk: does the group get bigger or smaller?

faq.q: How do Foundation students learn to add and subtract?
faq.a: They act out and draw everyday situations with objects, fingers and number lines, and use counting on, counting back or subitising (AC9MFN05). Symbols like + and − are not needed yet.
Starting from the first number and counting forward. For 5 and 3, say 5 in your head, then 6, 7, 8.

faq.q: Why does my child get 7 instead of 6 for 4 and 2?
faq.a: They may be counting the starting number again (4, 5, 6, 7). Show that you start on 4 and then count 2 more: 5, 6.

faq.q: How can I practise adding and taking away at home?
faq.a: Use snacks, toys or bath toys: put out 5, add 2, ask how many now. Eat or hide some and ask how many are left.
